headline: New York pauses giant AI data centers

sources.title: New York to impose the country's first statewide moratorium on data centers
New York becomes first state to impose data center moratorium
First Statewide Moratorium on New Hyperscale Data Centers Launched by Governor Kathy Hochul

chunks.text: New York has become the first American state to {{put off}} the building of giant data centers. On July 14, 2026, Governor Kathy Hochul {{signed off on}} a one-year pause on new permits for these huge buildings. The facilities are known as hyperscale data centers, and they run the [[servers]] behind AI and cloud [[computing]]. State leaders say they want time to study the effects before more of these centers open.

verbs.correct: To delay something until a later time
verbs.wrong: To stop something completely and for good

verbs.correct: To officially approve or agree to something
verbs.wrong: To finish a message or piece of work

chunks.text: The biggest worry is that these data centers {{use up}} huge amounts of electricity and water. The water helps keep the thousands of computers cool, since they run day and night. Many [[residents]] have {{spoken out}} because they fear the centers will {{drive up}} their [[utility]] bills. Officials are also worried about the extra pressure on the state's power [[grid]].

chunks.text: During the pause, state agencies will {{look into}} how the centers affect energy, water, and air quality. Experts will {{press ahead with}} a detailed environmental study before any new rules are made. The state also plans to {{set up}} guidelines so that nearby [[communities]] gain real benefits, like better local [[infrastructure]]. The moratorium only covers the largest projects, those that need 50 [[megawatts]] of power or more.

chunks.text: Some technology companies have {{pushed back}}, saying the pause could send new [[investment]] and jobs to other states. Even so, the governor refuses to {{back down}}, and she wants strong rules in place first. Dozens of cities and counties have already blocked such projects, but no state had {{weighed in}} until now. If the study goes well, building may {{go ahead}} again next year under stricter [[standards]].

tf.s: New York decided to put off building new hyperscale data centers for one year.
tf.why: The state put off new projects with a one-year pause so it can study their effects first.

tf.s: Governor Hochul quickly backed down and canceled the moratorium.
tf.why: The governor refused to back down; she kept the pause in place so she could set strong rules first.

tf.s: Officials say the data centers barely use up any electricity or water.
tf.why: The main worry is exactly the opposite: the centers use up huge amounts of electricity and water.

tf.s: During the pause, state agencies will look into how the centers affect energy, water, and air.
tf.why: Agencies will look into these effects and press ahead with a detailed study before any new rules are made.

tf.s: Many residents have spoken out because they fear higher utility bills.
tf.why: Residents spoke out over worries that the centers would drive up their utility bills.

tf.s: No cities or counties had weighed in on data centers before New York acted.
tf.why: Dozens of cities and counties had already blocked such projects; New York was just the first state to weigh in.
